comment: I am a resident of Salt lake county. I am writing to demand that the City Council adopt a budget for the people, that prioritizes community wellbeing and redirects funding away from the police. We are in the midst of widespread upheaval over the systemic violence of policing, embodied by the SLCPD?s well documented history of lethal force against residents of color. Empty gestures and suggestions of reform are unacceptable. I am demanding the voices of this movement be heard, and that real change be made to the way this city allocates its resources. Support for marginalized communities is necessary now, more than ever. But instead, the Mayor has proposed an increase in funding to the SLCPD, while social services and education--proven to better promote community safety than policing--stagnate. The SLCPD has seen a rise in overtime pay which, when too often paid out to officers responsible for harassing unhoused, Black, Indigenous, and Latinx residents, is deeply insulting. I am demanding that the City Council defund the SLCPD. I demand a budget that adequately and effectively meets the needs of impacted Utahans during this trying and uncertain time, when livelihoods are on the line. I demand a budget that supports community wellbeing, rather than empowering the policing forces that tear us apart. Although City Council has thus far avoided voting or revising Mayor Mendenhall's budget proposal, the document is back in your hands. It is your duty to represent your constituents. I am urging you to completely revise the SLC budget for 2020-2021 fiscal year, and to fund care, not criminalization and incarceration. You must adopt a budget that is for the people. Public opinion is with me. Thank you for your time, Elliot Bigler

We, the citizens of Utah and this great nation, fully support the first amendment right to free speech and PEACEFUL assembly. We as members of Utah Citizen?s Alarm are 100% inclusive and welcome and love our brothers and sisters of any race, religion or sexual orientation. We have been falsely painted as white supremacists? or racist?. Standing up to violence, lawlessness and destruction of our communities has NOTHING to do with race. The scourge of violent protests and civil unrest is a real and present danger. The unpredictability and potential for violence at these protests has been clearly demonstrated over and over again not only nationwide, but more recently in our own community. Thus, not only has law enforcement rightfully ramped up their efforts to be a ?show of force? and a massive deterrent to any violence or unrest, so now have the citizens of Utah banded together to protect our own communities from the threat of violence and anarchy. Dear Mayor Mendenhall and Salt Lake City Council, Many of us who are residents of Salt Lake City and the surrounding cities are concerned by your recent action and inaction regarding the safety of our community. You have a duty to protect Salt Lake City from violence, civil unrest and destruction and devaluation of property. If you collect tax revenue for stated purposes and then fail to support the objectives of those sources, you are in breach of duty and you subject the city to civil liability. Apologizing to the Carbajal family when you did was irresponsible, and was disloyal to your police department. While all of our hearts go out to the Carbajal family, those of us who are familiar with precedent case law in this specific area expected Sim Gill's conclusion, which was legally correct in every way. Apologizing for the correct actions of the police officers involved weakened your integrity as one that should put support of a good law enforcement agency as a top priority. You either had or should have had reasonable advance knowledge of the recent protests that affected Salt Lake City, particularly the first one where a police car was destroyed and other property was damaged. What did you do to protect your city, your citizens and your police department? All reports point to your tying the hands of the police department and facilitating a liberal agenda, which would include inciting unrest, similar to the actions of other Democrat politicians around the nation, in an effort to affect November elections in a rather counterfeit fashion. Last night, July 18th, protesters were allowed to gather in front of the governor of Utah's mansion, they illegally used their own cars to block traffic. City streets and access to businesses were shut down, allowing protesters to march from the governor's mansion to the State Capitol. Last week, you allowed protesters to unlawfully assemble, block traffic and cause hundreds of thousands of dollars of damage to the new D.A.'s office. Hear this loud and clear: Utah residents were and are disgusted with your lack of courage and leadership and for your inaction in allowing these things to happen and we will not stand for it. Salt Lake City is not Seattle. It is not Los Angeles. We are better than that, and need to behave better than what we have seen from other cities, where the leadership is determined to destroy whom and what they have stewardship over, in an effort to push a political agenda. You have been granted a sacred duty to serve and protect the citizens, not a political party, an agenda, or a personal vision. Your legacy as a mayor is for you to shape. You can be remembered and revered as an effective leader of a great community, or you can be remembered as a disgrace, where years of disaster cleanup followed your administration. Please put the great people of Salt Lake City and the surrounding communities first. Politics are insignificant compared to the personal and financial security of our residents. Please show the people of our community that your priorities are in the right place. Truly responsible leadership, that which is driven by a love for the people and not loyalty to a cause, is always rewarded at re-election time. If you wish to continue to serve, please help our community by doing the right things as mayor. Regards Kenneth Nielson

Dear Council Member Dugan, Each day I drive into Salt Lake City where I work as a manager of a business in Salt Lake City, and have become increasingly concerned about my personal safety and the safety of the business I manage in Salt Lake City. Myself, other members of the business community, and concerned citizens are watching your response to violence and to the destruction and damage to public and private property. Although I appreciate your service to the community in the many areas you are handling well, it is clear that there is something amiss in the way the city is handling these outbreaks of violence. The following are specific concerns that I feel need to be addressed: 1) Please do everything in your power to support law and order by letting your police officers know that they have your support. We as a community cannot afford for the police department to be tepid in their response to violent and destructive acts due to unclear directives from your office. 2) Please give clear directives to the police to immediately arrest INDIVIDUALS who initiate acts of violence against other citizens; or the destruction of public and private property. For example, in the recent riot that broke out in front of the attorney general?s office, it was reprehensible that the police and city officials watched while vandalism ensued. Surely when the first can of red paint was opened and applied to the building, arrests should have been made. In an earlier protest when police cars were lit on fire, the perpetrators should have been immediately arrested, the gathering declared unlawful and the vandals arrested. 3) Please give clear directives that public streets should remain open during protests. As you know citizens of our country have the right to peacefully assemble. However other members of the community have rights to not attend the protests, and must not have their rights to use and enjoy the public streets; or have access to their private property inhibited because your administration has surrendered the streets to unlawful activities. Inattention to these matters dishonors the citizens of this community. It particularly dishonors the law abiding citizens that are showing up to be involved in a peaceful protest, only to have their message tainted by the individuals perpetrating violence at these protests. Sincerely, Frank J Tervort

Dear Council Member Mano, My name is Jeff Kleinman and I am a resident of Salt Lake City District 5. In our neighborhood I see houseless people, people with addiction, and people with mental health crises every day. I believe that for the safety of Black, Indigenous, and communities of Color we need to start to disempower and disband the SLCPD and replace it with a combination of already existing community services, non-government organizations and new methods of community-focused transformative justice. We cannot replace the police with organizations that funnel people into the criminal justice system. The people that respond to emergency calls should not be able to arrest the people that they are serving. I believe that defunding the police and shifting that money to address inequity in the SLC budget, grant awarding, zoning, housing, and access to public programs is a way to start empowering communities that are subjugated by systemic racism. Thank you so much for your time Darin, Jeff
